**Remove from repo root and restructure for proper daily note workflow.**

This file violates vault daily-note infrastructure in three ways:

1. **Wrong location**: Daily notes must reside in `./daily_notes/` (per `daily_rollover.py` line 46), not the repo root.

2. **Templater syntax conflicts with automation**: Obsidian Templater syntax (`<%* ... %>` and `<% ... %>`) belongs in `DAILY NOTE TEMPLATE.md`. The `daily_rollover.py` automation generates and maintains **static** YAML frontmatter in daily note files; Templater syntax will be overwritten during the rollover process.

3. **Contradicts vault conventions**: Per `VAULT-CONVENTIONS.md` (lines 484 and 267–283), the workflow is:
   - Create from `DAILY NOTE TEMPLATE.md` (template contains Templater syntax)
   - Obsidian generates the daily note file
   - Automation (`daily_rollover.py`) maintains static YAML and carryforward logic

The `[[TO DO LIST]]` marker aligns with the automation's `extract_todo_section()` function, confirming intent to integrate with the rollover system—which requires static YAML and the correct directory location (`./daily_notes/`).

If this file is meant to be a reusable template, rename it to `DAILY NOTE TEMPLATE.md` and ensure it contains only Templater syntax. If it is a daily note for 2026-06-18, move it to `./daily_notes/2026-06-18.md` and replace Templater syntax with static YAML values.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the
rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate.

In `@2026-06-18.md` around lines 1 - 25, The file 2026-06-18.md is improperly
placed in the repo root and contains Templater syntax that conflicts with the
daily note automation workflow. Move this file from the repo root to
./daily_notes/2026-06-18.md and replace all Templater syntax expressions (the
<%* ... %> and <% ... %> blocks) with their static computed values for the date
2026-06-18. This ensures the daily note has static YAML frontmatter as expected
by the daily_rollover.py automation while maintaining the correct directory
structure per vault conventions.
```

</details>

`date created` and `date modified` are both derived from `d`, which is the date parsed from the file title (not the current time). This will always set the time to whatever default moment assigns (often midnight) and will also keep `date modified` from reflecting actual edits. Consider setting `date created` using the current timestamp (e.g., `moment()`) at generation time, and updating `date modified` via an automated update mechanism (editor/plugin) that runs on save rather than templating it from the title date.

For readability/consistency with common moment usage, add a space after the comma in `subtract(1, \"d\")` / `add(1, \"d\")` (i.e., `subtract(1, \"d\")` → `subtract(1, \"d\")` with proper spacing). This makes the template easier to scan and keeps formatting consistent with typical code style.

✅ Addressed in commits 6e28ceb to 7342e41

The fenced code block is labeled as `php` but the example is a shell snippet, and the example shown (`then...fi`) is not valid shell syntax as written. Update the fence language to `sh`/`bash` and format the conditional as a valid multi-line example (replacing the ellipsis with a comment or example commands).

This file embeds large blocks of external Terms & Conditions / license text and repeats them multiple times (per-platform download sections), resulting in a very large, highly duplicated document. Consider replacing the verbatim license content with a short note plus a link to the authoritative source, and de-duplicating the per-platform download sections (e.g., keep a single license section and list platform download links once). This will drastically reduce repo size and make future updates manageable.

The trailing `English (US)` line reads like scraped page metadata and doesn’t fit the rest of the note content. Remove it, or move it into frontmatter (e.g., a `language:` field) if it’s intended to be part of the note’s metadata.
Capitalize `android` to `Android` in the image alt text for consistency with platform naming.

This looks like a raw YouTrack export artifact: repeated standalone `N` lines and lots of spacing reduce readability. Consider converting these sections into proper Markdown lists or tables (e.g., `- [IJPL-39532](...) — ...`) and removing the stray `N` markers so the note is scannable.
